1ayjqt4: Two frames: the main verb sets the tense
mlpxe9: If the verb that asks, wishes, evaluates or needs is in the present, future, imperative or present perfect, the subjunctive goes in the present. If it is in a past tense (preterite, imperfect, pluperfect) or in the conditional, the subjunctive goes in the imperfect. The same happens after «para que», «antes de que» and «cuando» with future meaning.
fmmfng: Watch out for the conditional: even though it talks about the future, it belongs to the past frame. «Me gustaría que vinieras», not «me gustaría que vengas», in the most widespread standard.

f6zl8m: Looking back from now: perfect and imperfect
18p9gf3: From a main verb in the present you can also talk about something earlier. If that action is close to the present or its result is still alive, use the perfect subjunctive: «me alegra que hayan votado tantas personas». If it is a closed past, with a marker such as «ayer» or «el año pasado», use the imperfect: «me alegra que votaran tantas personas el año pasado».
1m9ib9j: The two-frame rule has a useful exception: if someone asked for something in the past and that content is still pending, the present is also accepted: «la concejala pidió que mandemos el plano esta semana».

1q1kd9d: «Si»: a possible plan or an imagined world
1s9x1kv: With «si + present indicative» you present an open condition: you believe it can be fulfilled and you set up a real consequence in the present, future or imperative. With «si + imperfect subjunctive» you distance the condition from the current reality, and the consequence goes in the simple conditional. The choice depends not only on the facts but on how the speaker sees them.
ac7vmh: Although it is called «imperfect», in these sentences the subjunctive does not talk about the past: it talks about now or the future. And the order is free: you can start with the consequence without changing the tenses. When «si» comes first, separate the two parts with a comma.

xxc58d: Hypotheses are very useful for making cautious proposals: «si pusiéramos el taller junto al muelle, ¿no sería más visible?». 1xl517e: Original SpanishCue text in the form of a newsletter from a fictional residents' association in Rosario. The data and people are invented.
svegxs: Dear neighbours: as every September, the City Council has opened the call for participatory budgeting. This year the rules changed a little. Until 2024 they required each proposal to have fifty signatures; now they require us to gather a hundred and to submit three quotes from different companies. The committee also asked us to keep the project under ten per cent of the district fund. We think this is reasonable, although it forces us to work faster.
ht0hnf: Our proposal is a bike workshop on the riverside. If we get the signatures before the twentieth, the committee will review the project in October and, if it approves it, the neighbourhood will be able to vote on it in November. We want all residents to know about it before that date, which is why we are organising a talk at the club on Thursday. It is important that people who don't ride a bike come too: we also need their opinion.
19ipjdj: We allow ourselves to dream a little. If the workshop worked well for a year, we could ask the council to include it in its permanent programme. If we also found experienced volunteers, we would run mechanics courses for older adults. And if the river didn't rise so much every autumn, which is a lot to ask, we would keep the bikes stored by the water instead of taking them to the club's shed.
ym7npj: Not everyone agrees, and it is good that it should be so. At the last meeting, some residents preferred the money to go towards lighting the inner streets of the neighbourhood. We are glad they raised it openly. We propose that both ideas be submitted and that the vote decides. What we don't want is for the neighbourhood to end up without a project because we didn't agree in time.
1mbch2m: One last practical request. The committee has reminded us that the signature sheets must be complete, without crossings-out and with each resident's ID number. Last year several signatures were not counted because someone wrote their address instead of their ID number. We kindly ask you to check your details before signing, so that this year we don't lose a single supporter.
